facts.fact: HZD_RCU dispatch calls Rcu::quiet. User-return and VM-return paths check hazards; idle checks them before halt/mwait with interrupts enabled. This closes concrete quiescence callsites, not every latency condition: hazard processing still depends on actually reaching these paths and executing on the relevant CPU.

The timer handler invokes Timeout::check if expired and then Rcu::update. VEC_IPI_IDL routes to Ec::idl_handler, which calls Rcu::update(false) only when current continuation is Ec::idle. IPI send targets CPU/APIC topology. Successful IPI issuance or timer configuration is not an observed interrupt delivery, quiescent acknowledgment, completed batch or finalizer deadline.

Preemption control disables/enables interrupts; a preemption point briefly permits interrupts. CPU initialization registers a CPU through Hip::add_cpu on initial boot. HIP membership checks a bounded CPU descriptor flag. Runtime online-count/descriptor consistency, interrupt masking durations, startup/hotplug/suspend behavior and actual hardware remain configuration/timing obligations; this partial source is not a proof every batch participant responds within a numerical interval.

Scheduling selects the highest ready priority, tracks remaining budget and programs the budget timeout; disabled scheduling contexts may require repeated scheduling and RCU release. Timeout::check triggers all expired entries; callbacks and their count affect handler work. A timeslice/budget is not a global service, RPC, RCU or cleanup deadline, nor does it prove priority starvation or callback latency absent a complete bounded workload and hardware contract.

SC pre_free disables execution and sets scheduling hazard locally or sends remote recall IPI. Remote removal retains deferred reference state and uses a remote queue; its handler examines disable/partner/return-capability/continuation conditions before scheduling or RCU. free/free_xcpu delete only after removal/refcount eligibility. Pending cross-CPU work, partner references and deferred callbacks therefore survive a logical disable and need explicit accounting and completion witnesses.

EC pre_free removes UTCB mappings, flushes CPU state and may enqueue cross-CPU EC/SC finalization. free destroys only after reference release. Destruction includes return-capability, FPU/UTCB and virtualization-state cleanup; cross-CPU return signals the caller after scheduling transitions. These are real lifecycle paths, not a single synchronous all-free operation, and do not close all object/cache/device/provider debt.

LAPIC setup depends on CPU deadline support/command-line policy and calibrated or measured TSC/bus frequencies. Timer programming uses either countdown or TSC-deadline mode. Timeout code explicitly handles a TSC stopping in sleep by reprogramming the timer. Those mechanisms require an exact supported platform/clock/interrupt configuration before deriving a wall-clock progress bound.

Bootstrap adjusts root quota for kernel use, transfers four pages per online CPU into a reserve and sets a root nontransferable reserve. Halt preparation flushes VM/FPU state then shutdown follows. These source literals and shutdown paths must be included in full domain geometry; they neither establish a project-wide peak nor make shutdown/reboot a physical cleanup proof.

One supported topology must bound execution gates, interrupt delivery, queue/callback work, all references and physical backing together.

facts.fact: Quota tracks used, over, upli and notr. alloc increments usage; free reduces usage or records excess free credit in over and adjusts limit. boot deducts static kernel usage from the root limit. free_up moves remaining limit, usage and credits into another account and reconciles outstanding usage/credit. Thus account destruction is not simply usage zero or an unconditional newly-free physical pool; delayed-accounting debt must be followed.

transfer_to checks source limit and available balance including notr by default, debits source limit and credits destination, with over/used reconciliation. set_limit transfers upper budget then sets lower nontransferable reserve. PD-control validates PD capability types and returns failure for insufficient transfer. This is an explicit quota-transfer mechanism, not a per-transfer amount proving total epoch cap. Full initialization, call authority, allocator enforcement and arithmetic/concurrency invariants remain required.

A temporary guard obtains needed quota from its reference account with check_notr false and returns guard accounting via free_up on destruction. The local check/reserve mechanism and ordinary nontransferable reserve are distinct; the complete graph must include guarded allocation, temporary overlap and the bypassed reserve check rather than treating notr as an absolute barrier for every path. Buddy/slab allocator implementations are not in this selection.

Syscall checks may invoke OOM handling or return QUO_OOM. PD creation validates lower/upper values, checks source quota, allocates a PD, transfers limits and inserts its capability; failures delete the PD. PD deletion returns its account into the owning PD and frees its slab entry. Constructor/cache/page-table/refcount details outside selected files still matter to whole physical peak and failed-start cleanup.

call runs an optional pre-finalizer and enqueues deferred work. RCU uses per-CPU next/current/done queues, batch state and online-CPU quiescent counting before invoking finalizers. update can send idle IPIs when both queues are populated and a queue count exceeds2000; that threshold is not an admission cap. No clock deadline is present here. Progress requires update/quiet callsites, scheduling, interrupt and finalizer behavior beyond this partial source; no actual stall or leak was observed.

Revoke traverses/demotes mapping trees and queues removed nodes via RCU. Remote revoke retains/releases PD references and may enqueue a semaphore notification before returning success. PD pre_free revokes memory/PIO/object spaces and releases device RIDs; later free deletes only when references allow. The destructor clears page/IOMMU/nested/local tables and caches. Referenced implementations and hardware synchronization are not all included: success is not proof that all finalizers, DMA or physical backing have settled within a numeric bound.

README identifies patches required for the Genode-adjusted kernel. IOAPIC and Intel-IOMMU patches comment out removal of relevant device memory regions to permit platform-driver access. IOMMU patch skips interrupt-cache invalidation when current queue base differs from the kernel-owned queue. MSI patch adds a nonzero dev guard to device-cap validation. These are textual changes to device-authority paths, not proof of a configured denial boundary, safe DMA quiescence or an applied/build-tested patch set.

QPD decodes scheduling quantum and priority; it is not the memory-quota object. Keeping that distinction prevents an inspected scheduling descriptor from being counted as evidence of memory or cleanup enforcement.

Buddy initializes a finite physical pool with block-head/index overhead and page-rounded free range. _alloc holds allocator lock, selects/splits an order-aligned block, optionally fills memory, then charges2^order pages via quota.alloc. It does not itself check quota.hit_limit before allocating. alloc searches pools and panics on exhausted physical availability. _free returns quota before coalescing under allocator lock. This is backing geometry and accounting source, not a proof all callsites pre-reserve or that a quota balance equals every instantaneous physical byte.

Slab growth allocates a full buddy page; per-element size includes rounded payload/link/alignment and page header overhead. Allocation holds cache lock and grows when no current slab exists, without its own quota admission check. Element release can retain an empty slab for reuse; selected extra empty slabs are destroyed and whole-cache free destroys pages. Live-element count therefore differs from page allocation, retained empties and deferred-finalizer overlap. Source assertions/call order do not provide a deadline or a complete resource-conservation proof.
